newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Healthscope to build A$12.7 mln hospital.
newsitem.headline: Healthscope to build A$12.7 mln hospital.

text.p: Hospitals group Healthscope Ltd said on Tuesday it would spend A$12.7 million to construct a new 65 bed private hospital on the grounds of the Modbury Public Hospital in Adelaide which it currently administered.

Healthscope deputy chairman Richard England said in a statement the company had also signed a new management contract with the public hospital board to enable it "to stem the losses" incurred since taking over management in February 1995.

England warned Healthscope did not expect to ever make a substantial profit from the Modbury contract because of the discount payable to the South Australian government, but it expected to be close to break-even in 1997/98.

"As a result, we are now in a position to develop the new Torrens Valley Private Hospital, which was one of the terms of our intitial agreement with the State government for the running of the Modbury public hospital," he said.

Healthscope, which operates 12 private hospitals in South Australia, Victoria, Tasmania and the Northern Territory, as well as managing the Modbury public hospital, said it expected the private Modbury facility to be operating within two years.
